newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to sell 440.62 mln shares in Chiao Tung.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to sell 440.62 mln shares in Chiao Tung.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry said on Wednesday it would sell 440.62 million shares or 28.8 percent in Chiao Tung Bank in early August, accelerating the state-owned bank's privatisation.
The move would reduce state's stake in Chiao Tung Bank to 60.03 percent from 88.83 percent.
The finance ministry said it planned to sell the bank's shares through an open auction. It gave no details of how or when the auction would be held.
Chiao Tung Bank was listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange on September 25, 1996.
On Wednesday, Chiao Tung Bank ended down T$3.5 or 4.4 percent at T$76.5.

Taiwan's government said in January it planned to release some 800 million state-owned shares worth some T$100 billion in fiscal 1997/98 (July/June) to get out of industry and help alleviate its budget deficit.
Listed in the plan was the goal of selling off 634 million shares, or 48.8 percent, of Chiao Tung Bank.
It gave no exact dates for the sales or other details.

The finance ministry said in July that the government's privatisation scheme would accelerate from the middle of 1998, outlining plans to release state-owned shares worth T$450 billion over the next three fiscal years.
State shares worth T$150 billion would be released in fiscal 1998/99 (July-June), it said without giving details.
